ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the length of line segment $AD$ is 30 cm, and points $C$ and $B$ are both on line segment $AD$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$. The length of $AE$ is 12 cm. If $AC = \frac{1}{3} AD$, and point $F$ is the midpoint of line segment $CD$, find the length of line segment $EF$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
$\because AC= \frac{1}{3} AD= \frac{1}{3}\times30=10\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore CD=AD-AC=30-10=20\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\because$ Point F is the midpoint of line segment CD,\\
$\therefore DF=\frac{1}{2}CD=10\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore EF=AD-AE-DF=30-12-10=\boxed{8}\,\text{cm}$.

Point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and $AE=12$ cm. If $AC=\frac{1}{3}AD$, and point $F$ is the midpoint of line segment $CD$, find the length of line segment $EF$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows one straight horizontal line segment with labeled points arranged from left to right as A, C, E, B, D. Thus C and B lie on segment AD, and E is also shown on the same line between C and B. Reasoning following the coordinate method: Place A at coordinate 0 and D at coordinate 30, since AD = 30 cm. Because AC = (1/3)AD, AC = (1/3) × 30 = 10 cm, so C is at coordinate 10. Since AE = 12 cm, E is at coordinate 12. Point F is the midpoint of CD, so its coordinate is (10 + 30)/2 = 20. Therefore EF is the distance between coordinates 12 and 20, which is 20 - 12 = 8 cm.
